MultiNLI by Williams, Nangia and Bowman, distributed under the source-specific permissive terms described in the publisher's paper. Prompts have been reformatted; human gold relations are mapped to yes/no/maybe.
question: Does training a shared-depth decoder on human explanations and counterfactual hypothesis triplets improve completed language-inference judgments across caption and out-of-training-genre text, beyond mere output formatting?
training: One caption premise and one multi-genre premise per update, three human-written hypotheses with three distinct gold relations per premise. Human explanations when supplied, relation supervision otherwise. An additional raw language anchor per update. Use each premise once. Use the released original K2 arithmetic adapter as the initial weights. No donor at training or inference. Data selected before training by hash; evaluation premises excluded. No model-specific prompting, verifier or choice restriction at generation.
decision: 48 fresh questions in 16 complete three-way premise groups. Both receive identical zero-demo thinking IDs and greedy 1024-token cap. Alternate model order halfway. Require >=4 net correct visible answers, a gain on both sources, more fully correct triplets, increased three-way likelihood probe accuracy with the same separate probe prefix, elapsed generation <=Base and raw V3 NLL within +0.03. Blind-review completed unscored judgments prior to confirmation. A pass permits independent disjoint triplet replication and integrated long-context and retention checks; failure closes this checkpoint. Stop at registered resource guards.
